author: Declaration Desk
title: Sensex falls 319 points as inflation and oil weigh; rupee slips to 94.24
dek: The Nifty ended at 25,144, ending a three-day run of gains, after October inflation came in above the RBI's upper limit and Brent crude rebounded.
body:
Indian shares fell on Friday, with the BSE Sensex closing 318.56 points, or 0.39%, lower at 81,592.45 and the NSE Nifty 50 down 155.05 points, or 0.61%, at 25,144.30, according to market reports. Thursday's figures showing retail inflation at 6.09% in October, above the Reserve Bank's upper tolerance limit of 6%, revived expectations of tighter policy, and Brent crude rose back above $95 a barrel after attacks on Saudi oil routes were reported.

Every sector index except FMCG ended lower, with auto, metal and realty shares down about 1%, one report said. Shriram Finance, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles and Grasim were the biggest Nifty losers; Eicher Motors, Hindustan Unilever and Bharti Airtel gained. Losers outnumbered gainers on the BSE by 2,328 to 1,763.

The fall ended a three-session winning run, according to most reports; one report described a longer streak. Over the week, the Nifty still rose about 0.5% and the Sensex about 0.7%, a third straight weekly gain.

The rupee closed at 94.24 to the dollar, 21 paise weaker than on Thursday. Foreign portfolio investors bought shares worth a net Rs 7,831 crore on Thursday, their ninth straight session of buying, according to provisional exchange data; figures for Friday were not yet available.
